channel.title: Koshin Studio — Notes (English)
channel.description: Development logs from building browser games and an iOS app, with measured numbers

item.title: How bullet-hell patterns work: ring, aimed, rain, spiral and homing, with formulas and live demos
item.description: The exact math behind ring, aimed (odd vs even), rain, spiral and homing bullet-hell patterns, from a real danmaku game, with live demos.

item.title: Sushi Stack scores stopped reaching the leaderboard: I changed the game’s numbers and forgot the server’s re-check (twice)
item.description: Honest runs of a browser game stopped reaching the online leaderboard: two game values changed without updating the server that re-checks scores. The fix, and a test that compares both sides with the same seeds.

item.title: Japanese Pokémon card & TCG lottery apps compared: Toreca Dash, Toreget, NowPokeca, Pokeka Tracker and Toreca no Chizu
item.description: Five apps and sites that track Pokémon card and TCG lotteries, pre-orders and restocks at stores in Japan, compared on games, alerts, maps and price — by the developer of one of them, weak points included.

item.title: The same report for the third time: a SwiftUI button responded only on its text, and my two earlier “fixes” did nothing
item.description: The “Won” and “Lost” buttons responded only on the text. Two earlier fixes (modifier order) did not work; I built the look inside a ButtonStyle and replaced six places. A mail-order article with coordinates had the same kind of root.

item.title: A function named “load from iCloud if newer” compared nothing: a 20-record history could become 1
item.description: The iCloud sync function never checked whether data was newer and replaced everything. A fresh device with an empty state could overwrite another device’s 20 records with 1. I added update-time comparison and never overwrite with empty.

item.title: With no ads, 25 real-device checks were blocked: test ads in developer mode only, and no hard-coded prize names
item.description: Before ads were served, 25 of 163 real-device checklist items could not be verified. In developer mode only, the app switches to Google’s test ad units. Prize names are read from one setting and never hard-coded, including in the checklist.

item.title: Online play that trusts nothing the client says: the server decides moves, clocks and results
item.description: Online play without login. Moves are validated by the rules engine, the clock lives only on the server, a disconnect gets 30 seconds, tokens are signed with HMAC, and ratings use pre-match numbers. With real values from the server code.

item.title: Setting the rules of Negaeri Shogi by playing AI against AI: one change that worked, six that broke
item.description: A 6×6 board game where sandwiched pieces defect. Instead of guessing the numbers, I ran 40 to 100 AI-vs-AI games per rule. Flips per move went from 2% to 81%, removing the king guard ended games in 17 moves, and the first-move edge is still unsolved.

item.title: Four store-matching mistakes in a TCG lottery app: spelling variants, vague map lookups, shared entry pages, and one page with many products
item.description: Four real cases where matching store names went wrong in a trading-card lottery app: spelling variants, a map lookup that returned Shizuoka, one entry page used by different stores, and one form for six products.

item.title: Seven records of cutting misses in crawling and monitoring: pagination, X monitoring, measuring coverage and waiting rooms
item.description: Seven records of counting and cutting misses while crawling and monitoring lottery and first-come sales: aggregator pagination, gaps in X monitoring, how coverage was measured, intervals vs delivery, and waiting-room pages.

item.title: Nine things that happened running scheduled jobs and a server: timeouts, time budgets, re-runs on deploy and a VPS migration
item.description: Nine records from the jobs that run hourly and daily, and the server under them: moving from Cloud Functions to a VPS, a timeout fixed three times, checks that never ran, re-runs on every deploy, and secrets in logs.

item.title: Pokémon card sleeves and loaders: sizes and what “pt” means
item.description: What to check before buying Pokémon card sleeves, toploaders and deck boxes: standard vs small size, what 35pt means, and a buying checklist. Not a hands-on review; unverified points are listed.

item.title: ITMS-91064 “Invalid Binary”: NSPrivacyTracking was true but NSPrivacyTrackingDomains was empty
item.description: An iOS build was rejected by Apple's automated review with ITMS-91064. NSPrivacyTracking was true while NSPrivacyTrackingDomains was an empty array. How it was fixed, and what was not verified.

item.title: Firebase 12 does not work with Xcode 15.2 (Swift 6.0 required): why I pinned Firebase 11.4.0 and AdMob 11.5.0
item.description: On an old Mac stuck on Xcode 15.2, newer Firebase and AdMob SDKs fail to build. Which versions break, which I pinned (Firebase 11.4.0, AdMob 11.5.0), and why.

item.title: iOS app freezes and is killed (0x8BADF00D): a SwiftUI computed property ran on every redraw
item.description: An iOS app was force-quit by the watchdog (0x8BADF00D). A SwiftUI computed property re-filtered and re-sorted 951 articles on the main thread every body evaluation.

item.title: No builds arriving in TestFlight: I had used up the 25 free Xcode Cloud hours (my first diagnosis was wrong)
item.description: New builds stopped appearing in TestFlight. My first diagnosis (“[ci skip] is blocking builds”) was wrong; the workflow built the iOS app on every commit.

item.title: Firebase Auth: force-quitting the app created anonymous accounts in bulk (waiting for currentUser to restore)
item.description: Force-quitting the app made Firebase create a new anonymous account each launch: 17 of 19 users were throwaway. Cause: reading currentUser too early.

item.title: A canvas becomes twice as large on Retina: inset:0 does not stretch it (a bug in a logo that bursts when you tap it)
item.description: Burst particles appeared in the wrong place on high-DPI screens. A canvas with only inset:0 keeps its pixel size, so it was 2x larger in CSS on Retina.

item.title: Making a 10-second stopwatch ranking fair: 3 decimals, ties and write counts
item.description: Why I truncate to three decimals so coarse clocks get no advantage, how ties (a 1/333 chance) are broken, and how I counted KV writes on the free tier.

item.title: From 16,177 titles to 6,091: how the anime quiz database was built by dropping over 60%
item.description: An anime quiz picks from about 6,000 titles. Where they came from, the criterion that cut 62.3% of 16,177, what remains, and the biases of the method.

item.title: “80% was chosen over 82%”: the quiz’s match percentage disagreed with its ranking
item.description: An anime quiz’s match percentage used a different yardstick from its ranking. With the old display, 35 to 40% of 1,000 synthetic respondents saw a reversed top 3.

item.title: The streaming buttons were shown even for titles you could not watch: making the quiz result screen true
item.description: The anime quiz showed the same two streaming buttons for every title; about 29% were wrong. How I narrowed buttons by availability and fixed image problems.

item.title: Cutting six buttons to one: first-time players did not know what to press
item.description: A browser game title screen had six things to press. I made the first step one button, and fixed saves vanishing inside an iframe and play continuing in a hidden tab.

item.title: Measuring Qiita’s “posting too frequently” limit: a new account could not create another article for about 30 minutes
item.description: After publishing, a new Qiita account could not create the next article. Checking the editor every 5 minutes, two measurements gave about 30 minutes; one was lost.

item.title: Rejected by CrazyGames with no reason given: I recorded the game and found four problems
item.description: A game portal rejected my game with only “overall quality below expectations.” I recorded what the reviewer saw, found four causes and fixed them by measuring.

item.title: Japanese text garbled in the CrazyGames preview: the file was correct, the cause was never found, so I escaped to ASCII
item.description: One character broke in a game portal’s preview though the file bytes were correct. How I made the game immune without finding the cause.

item.title: Works on my machine, breaks when deployed: four incidents shipping a static site to Cloudflare Pages
item.description: Stale cache, breadcrumbs that multiplied each build, a symlink into my own environment, and local-only images: four deploy incidents on Cloudflare Pages.

item.title: Comparing static site hosts by their official terms: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages and Firebase Hosting
item.description: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages and Firebase Hosting compared by official terms (Oct 2026): ads allowed, free limits, file limits, config.

item.title: Comparing comment systems for static sites by their official information: giscus, utterances, Disqus, Remark42 and more
item.description: giscus, utterances, Disqus, Remark42, Cusdis, Staticman and Commento compared by official pages (Oct 2026): storage, ads and tracking, maintenance status.

item.title: Comparing iOS ad SDKs and Firebase by their official information: AdMob, AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay and Supabase
item.description: AdMob, AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay, Firebase and Supabase compared by official pages (Oct 2026): payouts, privacy manifests, minimum Xcode, free tiers.

item.title: Claude API vs Gemini API by official numbers: small-model prices, web search, spend limits and deprecation
item.description: Claude and Gemini API compared by official pages (Oct 2026): small-model prices, web search cost and caps, spend limits, deprecation notice.

item.title: I could not listen, so I measured the waveform: building Japanese instruments with WebAudio for Sushi Stack
item.description: A browser game with no audio files: koto, taiko and gong synthesized with WebAudio. I could not listen, so I set volume by measuring waveform peaks.

item.title: Making a ranking server use only half of the free tier: from 5 calls to 2
item.description: A game ranking on Workers and D1: calls per play from 5 to 2, rows read from 421 to 221. Server-side rank counting and removing the preflight call.

item.title: Eight product-matching failures in a TCG lottery app: English vs katakana, splitting sets, official catalogs and spreading typos
item.description: Eight real failures in matching trading-card lottery articles to products: English vs katakana names, splitting 9-pack sets, products seeded from official catalogs, spreading typos, and leaked values.

item.title: Seven silent failures: real lotteries discarded, pages never read, and errors swallowed without a trace
item.description: Seven real cases where nothing raised an error yet real data was being dropped or never read: regexes, dates without a year, truncated AI answers, t.co relays, notice pages, swallowed try? failures, and fail-open.

item.title: Seven lessons from repairing bad data: existing records, bulk-job accidents, counting duplicates and the notification gate
item.description: Seven real lessons from repairing bad data: fixing the gate does not fix existing data, cleanup can hide entry bugs, a bulk job that hit everything, how duplicates were counted, and notifications that cannot be undone.

item.title: Where App Store review stopped me: “Guideline 2.1 Information Needed” on the first submission, and four rejections
item.description: Records of an indie iOS app stuck in App Store review: the six items asked for in Guideline 2.1 Information Needed on the first submission, and four rejections including iPad screenshots.

item.title: Python splitlines() breaks JSONL: the culprit was U+2028, an invisible line separator
item.description: Python splitlines() broke a JSONL file because 2 of 7,247 records contained U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR). Why it happens and the one-line fix: split on the newline only.

item.title: What changes when an anime quiz goes from 50 questions to 12?
item.description: A 50-question anime quiz now gives a result after 12. Measured with 1,000 synthetic respondents: the type mostly matches, but the single recommended title changes a lot.

item.title: “The pile settles at 89%” was wrong: my measurement was what was wrong
item.description: Rebalancing a merge puzzle, I found my measurement had counted falling pieces. Three causes: a backward size ladder, a pit-shaped tub, and pieces tunneling the floor.

item.title: Measuring the gap between ads in time, not in plays
item.description: Why I replaced “one ad every 5 plays” with “7 minutes since the last ad” in a browser game, how it behaves, and what I still do not know.

item.title: Five records of measuring, then cutting, AI and Firestore costs: a broken Gemini meter, 91% of reads in one place, and crawl costs
item.description: Five records of cutting AI (Claude, Gemini), Firestore and crawling costs in an indie app: doubting the meter first, converting to yen, and counting where the money actually went.

item.title: The conger eel was too big: finding why a merge puzzle’s last piece was out of reach
item.description: I could never reach my puzzle’s last piece. Statistics from hundreds of auto-played games showed the real cause: everything was too big for the tub.
